meta.label: Mental-health apps
meta.attribution: These are the ways a person in the United States or the United Kingdom gets help with their mental health from a phone or a phone line: four subscription or insurance-billed online therapy services (BetterHelp, Talkspace, Cerebral, Headspace), an insurance marketplace for booking therapists (Grow Therapy), a nonprofit sliding-scale therapist network (Open Path), the free NHS route in England (NHS Talking Therapies), self-help and tracking apps (Wysa's AI chatbot, MindDoc, Daylio, How We Feel, the VA's PTSD Coach, the Stay Alive safety-plan app), peer support (7 Cups and NAMI Connection groups), and the free crisis lines (988, Samaritans, Shout and Crisis Text Line). Method: privacy comes from each service's current privacy policy and its Apple App Store privacy label, scored lowest where data is used to track you or shared for advertising, and lower again where the FTC has acted (BetterHelp's 2023 order and Cerebral's 2024 order, both over health data shared with advertisers). Safety measures clinical oversight and crisis handling: who you actually talk to (licensed clinicians, supervised crisis counselors, trained volunteers, an AI, or nobody), what the service says it does in an emergency, and public enforcement such as Cerebral's 2024 federal non-prosecution agreement over controlled-substance prescribing. Cost uses each service's own price page or App Store in-app prices; free routes score 100. Accessibility counts hours, channels (phone, text, chat, no-smartphone and no-insurance routes), languages and the accessibility features declared on the App Store. We do not score whether a treatment works for you, and an app's privacy label is the developer's own declaration. Woebot's consumer app (closed June 2025) and Sanvello (no 2026 listing or working site found) are left out. Sources: the FTC, the US Attorney for the Eastern District of New York, the SEC, the VA, SAMHSA, the FCC, NHS England and nhs.uk, the services' own policy and price pages, and the Apple App Store. Not medical advice. If you are in crisis, call or text 988 in the US; in the UK call 111 and choose the mental health option, or Samaritans free on 116 123; call 911 or 999 if life is at risk. Reviewed 2026-10. Dispute or correct any rating via Contribute.

criteria.label: Keeps your mental-health data away from advertisers
Cost to you (free routes score highest)
Easy to reach: hours, channels, languages, no insurance needed

products.name: BetterHelp
products.description: The largest subscription therapy platform, matching you with a licensed counselor for messaging, chat, phone or video sessions. The FTC ordered it in 2023 to stop sharing health data for advertising and to pay $7.8 million after it passed sign-up answers to Facebook, Snapchat, Criteo and Pinterest.

privacy.note: The FTC's BetterHelp refund page says BetterHelp 'promised to keep users' information private but revealed data to Facebook, Snapchat, Pinterest, and Criteo for advertising purposes', including email addresses, IP addresses and answers to health questions; the July 2023 final order bans it from sharing health data for advertising and required $7.8 million for refunds, and a second round of payments went out in April 2025. Today BetterHelp's privacy policy (effective October 14, 2026) says that if you opt in to advertising cookies, some visitor data, excluding activity once you are logged in and in therapy, may still be shared for advertising, and its App Store privacy label lists location and usage data as used to track you across other companies' apps and websites.

safety.note: BetterHelp's FAQ says every therapist must be a licensed psychologist, LMFT, LCSW, LPC, LMHC or similar, with 'at least 3 years of experience' and 1,000 hours of hands-on practice, and that fewer than a third of applicants are accepted. It also says BetterHelp is not the right solution if 'You are in an urgent crisis or an emergency situation', and that messaging is not a good option in an emergency because a therapist may not see it for some time.

economical.note: BetterHelp's FAQ says self-pay therapy 'ranges from $70 to $100 per week' depending on location and therapist availability, billed as a membership you can cancel; the homepage says eligible insured members pay an average copay of $23 per session, though insurance may not appear as an option in every sign-up.

accessibility.note: BetterHelp offers live video, phone and chat sessions plus messaging for self-pay members (video only when using insurance), and its App Store listing is available in English, Dutch, French, German and Spanish. It is not for minors (teen therapy is a separate service) or for anyone without a reliable internet connection, and the app declares no accessibility features.

links.label: FTC: final order banning BetterHelp from sharing health data for advertising (July 2023)
BetterHelp on the App Store (privacy label)

products.name: Talkspace
products.description: Online therapy and psychiatry by video, voice or messaging with clinicians licensed in your state, mostly billed through US health insurance. Hospital operator Universal Health Services completed its purchase of Talkspace in August 2026.

privacy.note: Talkspace's privacy policy (last updated July 17, 2025) says it may disclose persistent identifiers to 'advertising technology vendors, third-party advertising networks, and social media platforms' for personalized advertising, marketing and analytics, and offers an opt-out of targeted advertising. Its App Store privacy label declares no data used to track you, with purchase history and user ID linked to you, including for its own advertising or marketing.

safety.note: Talkspace says your provider 'will be credentialed and licensed to practice in your state', offers psychiatry and medication management alongside therapy, and its site tells anyone in a life-threatening situation not to use the service but to call 988.

economical.note: Talkspace says most major insurance plans cover its therapy, typically for a copay of about $15 and often $0, that many employers cover it through an employee assistance plan, and that out-of-pocket plans 'begin at $69/week'.

accessibility.note: Universal Health Services' August 2026 filing announcing the completed acquisition says Talkspace serves people across all 50 states, Washington, D.C., and Puerto Rico through about 6,000 licensed providers, available to more than 200 million people through health plans; Talkspace also lists Medicare and Medicare Advantage coverage. The app is English-only and declares no accessibility features on the App Store.

links.label: UHS completes acquisition of Talkspace (SEC 8-K exhibit, August 2026)
Talkspace on the App Store (privacy label)

products.name: Cerebral
products.description: Online therapy and psychiatric medication management, by subscription or insurance. Cerebral settled FTC charges in 2024 over sharing nearly 3.2 million people's health data with advertisers and making cancellation hard, and signed a 2024 non-prosecution agreement with federal prosecutors over its past controlled-substance prescribing.

privacy.note: The FTC's May 2025 refund announcement summarizes its allegations that Cerebral 'disclosed consumers' sensitive personal health information and other sensitive data to third parties for advertising purposes' and kept billing people who asked to cancel; its April 2024 complaint said tracking tools passed data on nearly 3.2 million people to firms including LinkedIn, Snapchat and TikTok, and the settlement bans Cerebral from using health information for most advertising. Cerebral's current privacy policy still says it uses information to advertise its services on other parties' websites, subject to opt-outs, and its App Store privacy label lists identifiers as used to track you across other companies' apps and websites.

safety.note: Cerebral's site says its care comes from 600+ therapists and prescribers and that it treats with therapy and medication management. In November 2024 the US Attorney for the Eastern District of New York announced a non-prosecution agreement under which Cerebral forfeited $3,652,000 for practices that encouraged the unauthorized distribution of controlled substances such as Adderall from 2019 to 2022, including internal metrics that pushed prescribing; a further $2,922,000 fine was deferred because of the company's finances. The FTC's 2024 complaint also described former employees keeping access to medical records. We score below the other clinician-led services for this record.

economical.note: Cerebral's own FAQ lists self-pay prices of $180 every three months for a medication plan (medication billed separately) and $175 per therapy session or $795 for three months, says it accepts insurance in many plans, and says out-of-network sessions cost at most $405.

accessibility.note: Cerebral says it is available in all 50 states, accepts insurance and HSA/FSA cards, and offers same-day appointments in some states; its app is English-only, rated 18+, and declares no accessibility features on the App Store.

links.label: FTC: proposed order banning Cerebral from using health data for advertising (April 2024)
FTC: more than $5 million in Cerebral refunds (May 2025)
US Attorney EDNY: Cerebral non-prosecution agreement (November 2024)
Cerebral on the App Store (privacy label)

products.name: Headspace (therapy and coaching)
products.description: The meditation brand also sells video therapy with licensed therapists, mental health coaching and an AI companion inside the same app, paid through insurance, an employer, or out of pocket.

privacy.note: Headspace's privacy policy (effective September 30, 2026) says 'Headspace is not a data broker and does not sell your personal information to third parties for payment', but that it uses personal information 'To personalize the advertisements you receive about our Platform through third-party platforms' and works with third-party advertising platforms; residents of several states can opt out of targeted advertising. Its App Store label declares no data used to track you, with health, purchase, location and usage data linked to you, including for its own advertising or marketing.

safety.note: Headspace says its therapy is with licensed therapists by video, and its FAQ says that if you are 'in crisis, need immediate help, or are experiencing severe mental health symptoms, in-person or emergency care may be more appropriate'. The same app also offers an AI companion, Ebb, which is not a clinician.

economical.note: Headspace's therapy cost estimator shows typical in-network copays from $0 to about $25 a session for many plans, but says cost may reach up to $149 a session depending on coverage; the app's own App Store listing gives the meditation subscription as $12.99 a month or $69.99 a year.

accessibility.note: Headspace's therapy page lists dozens of in-network insurers, including some Medicaid plans, and accepts FSA/HSA and self-pay; therapy is US-only, and the app is listed in English with no accessibility features declared on the App Store.

links.label: Headspace on the App Store (privacy label)

products.name: Grow Therapy
products.description: A marketplace for booking in-network therapists and psychiatric prescribers through US health insurance, with an AI between-session coach in its app.

privacy.note: Grow Therapy's App Store privacy label declares no data used to track you, but lists contact details for its own advertising or marketing and links health, contact, financial and usage data to you; its website's cookie notice says it shares information with partners for advertising and analytics purposes.

safety.note: Grow Therapy's App Store listing describes therapy and medication support with insurance-covered providers, and says its AI coach 'isn't monitored in real time, and isn't a crisis tool', telling users in a crisis or emergency to call 988 or 911; the website footer gives the same advice.

economical.note: Grow Therapy's homepage says sessions average $21 with insurance and are HSA/FSA eligible, and its App Store listing says it accepts 100+ plans with no subscriptions or hidden fees; it is built around insurance, so people without coverage get less from it.

accessibility.note: Grow's listing advertises evening and weekend sessions, no waitlists and search by identity, specialty and language, but the app is English-only, rated 18+, and declares no accessibility features.

links.label: Grow Therapy on the App Store (privacy label)

products.name: Wysa
products.description: An AI chatbot for low mood, stress and anxiety built on cognitive behavioural techniques, usable anonymously, with optional paid sessions with human coaches. It is also offered through some NHS Talking Therapies services and employers.

privacy.note: Wysa's privacy policy says 'We do not share or sell your information, messages, or how you use our apps to advertisers or companies that buy data', that only derived and anonymous data is sent to a third-party language model for weekly reports, and that it uses Meta Ads Manager to run its own ads. Its App Store label lists only data not linked to your identity.

safety.note: Wysa's FAQ says its conversational replies are all AI-generated, that it is 'not recommended for crisis situations' or for people with severe and enduring mental health problems, and that its paid human coaches hold master's degrees in psychology or social work or coaching certification rather than being licensed therapists. It scores above self-tracking apps for clinical design and below services staffed by licensed clinicians.

economical.note: The AI chat is free; the App Store lists Wysa Premium from $9.99 a month to $74.99 a year and paid guided support with a coach from $29.99 a week.

accessibility.note: Wysa says it can be used 'Completely anonymous' and reports use in 105 countries; it is for ages 13 and over (11+ through some providers), the App Store listing is English-only, and no accessibility features are declared.

links.label: Wysa on the App Store (privacy label)

products.name: MindDoc
products.description: A German mood-monitoring and self-help app that asks short questions up to three times a day and suggests courses for depression, anxiety, insomnia and more. Its companion app is registered as a Class I medical device in the EU.

privacy.note: MindDoc's App Store privacy label lists identifiers and usage data as used to track you across other companies' apps and websites, and lists third-party advertising among the purposes for linked data, alongside health data and user content. Its website says it complies with the EU General Data Protection Regulation.

safety.note: MindDoc's website says the app was developed by psychologists, evaluated in a clinical study with more than 1,000 participants, and that the MindDoc Companion App is a Class I medical device under the EU Medical Device Regulation; it is self-guided, with no clinician reviewing your answers unless you take up MindDoc's separate online psychotherapy.

economical.note: The App Store lists MindDoc Plus and access plans from $4.49 a month to $69.99 for 12 months, with a 7-day trial on some plans.

accessibility.note: The app is available in English and German, is rated 16+, and declares no accessibility features on the App Store.

links.label: MindDoc on the App Store (privacy label)

products.name: Daylio
products.description: A mood journal: tap a mood and the day's activities, and the app charts patterns over time. Entries stay on your phone unless you back them up to your own cloud storage.

privacy.note: Daylio's website says 'We don't send your data to our servers so we don't have the access to your entries', that backups go to your own Google Drive or iCloud over encrypted channels, and that entries can be locked with a PIN or Face ID. Its App Store label lists only purchase, usage and diagnostic data, none of it linked to you.

safety.note: Daylio describes itself as a diary and mood tracker; nothing on its site describes clinical review, treatment, or crisis handling, so it offers no safety net if your mood is getting worse. Useful for noticing patterns to share with a clinician, not a substitute for one.

economical.note: Daylio is free to download and use; the App Store lists an optional Premium subscription from $4.99 a month to $35.99 a year, with some higher-priced options.

accessibility.note: The App Store lists Daylio in English and 46 other languages and says it supports VoiceOver and a dark interface; it runs on iOS and Android.

links.label: Daylio on the App Store (privacy label)

products.name: How We Feel
products.brand: The How We Feel Project, Inc.
products.description: A free emotion journal from a nonprofit whose science team is led by Marc Brackett of the Yale Center for Emotional Intelligence. You check in on how you feel, learn words for it, and try short regulation exercises.

privacy.note: How We Feel's privacy policy says it is a non-profit, 'We do not sell your personal information, and we do not use it to sell ads or make money', and that you can use the app without opening an account, in which case it collects no personal information. Check-in data goes to researchers only if you authorize it, anonymized; optional AI features send parts of a check-in to OpenAI.

safety.note: How We Feel describes itself as a journal for well-being created by scientists, designers, engineers and psychologists, with its scientific team led by the Yale Center for Emotional Intelligence; it is self-guided, with no clinician or crisis service behind it.

economical.note: How We Feel says the app is free and made possible by donations; the App Store lists no in-app purchases.

accessibility.note: The App Store lists How We Feel in English and Spanish with no accessibility features declared; its privacy policy says users must be at least 18.

links.label: How We Feel on the App Store

products.name: PTSD Coach
products.description: A free app from the VA National Center for PTSD for anyone living with symptoms after trauma, not only veterans: information, symptom screening and tracking, coping tools and links to support.

privacy.note: PTSD Coach's App Store privacy label lists only health, identifier, usage and diagnostic data that is not linked to your identity, used for analytics, and no tracking.

safety.note: The VA says PTSD Coach provides 'facts and self-help skills based on research', uses the PTSD Checklist, a validated self-report measure used across the VA and Department of Defense, but 'is not meant to replace professional care'; the app includes direct links for support and help.

economical.note: The VA describes PTSD Coach as 'a free and publicly available mobile app for anyone who wants to learn about and manage symptoms after a trauma'.

accessibility.note: The VA says PTSD Coach 'has now been downloaded over 1 million times in 115 countries' and is free for anyone, not only veterans; the App Store lists support for VoiceOver, larger text and differentiation without colour alone, but the app is English-only.

links.label: PTSD Coach (VA National Center for PTSD)
PTSD Coach on the App Store

products.name: Stay Alive
products.description: A free UK suicide-prevention app from a charity: build a personal safety plan, keep reasons for living, and find help, for people at risk and the people around them.

privacy.note: Stay Alive's App Store privacy label lists only usage data, not linked to your identity, used for analytics.

safety.note: Grassroots says Stay Alive was developed with 'clinical expertise from Sussex Partnership NHS Foundation Trust', consulting young people, LGBTQ adults and mental health professionals, that it is endorsed by the NHS, and that it won a Patient Safety Award in 2015. It is a self-help and signposting tool, not a monitored service.

economical.note: Grassroots says Stay Alive 'can be downloaded for free from the Google Play Store and Apple App Store', with a free web version.

accessibility.note: Stay Alive runs on Android, iOS and a web version for desktop and laptop computers, and Grassroots says updates have added new languages; the App Store lists it in English with no accessibility features declared.

links.label: Stay Alive on the App Store

products.name: 7 Cups
products.description: Free anonymous chat with trained volunteer listeners and peer support rooms, with an AI chatbot and paid online therapy as add-ons.

privacy.note: 7 Cups' App Store privacy label declares no data used to track you, but links health data, contact details, user content, identifiers and usage data to you and lists its own advertising or marketing among the purposes.

safety.note: 7 Cups says its free chat is with trained volunteer listeners, and its home page also promotes an AI counsellor and separate paid therapy with licensed therapists; the free listeners are not clinicians and the volunteer chat is not a crisis service.

economical.note: The listener chat and community are free; the App Store lists paid upgrades from $3.99 to $94.99 and a lifetime upgrade of $399.99, with therapy billed separately.

accessibility.note: 7 Cups says volunteer listeners are available 24/7 by anonymous online chat, with forums and scheduled group sessions; the app is English-only, rated 13+, and declares no accessibility features.

links.label: 7 Cups on the App Store (privacy label)

products.name: NAMI Connection support group
products.description: Free, peer-led recovery support groups for adults living with a mental health condition, run in person and online by the National Alliance on Mental Illness. A no-app route built on people with lived experience.

privacy.note: NAMI lists its Connection groups as 'Confidential'; there is no app collecting data, though you may register with a local affiliate to join.

safety.note: NAMI says groups are 'Led by people with mental health conditions' who are trained leaders, follow a structured model, and that 'No specific medical therapy or treatment is endorsed'; NAMI's pages direct anyone in crisis to call or text 988. Peer support, not clinical care.

economical.note: NAMI says the groups are 'Free of cost to participants'.

accessibility.note: NAMI says groups meet weekly, every other week or monthly depending on location, that 'Many support groups are virtual and attendance is open to everyone across the country', and that a Spanish version runs in a limited number of states; groups are for adults 18+. NAMI also runs a HelpLine at 800-950-6264.

products.name: Open Path Collective
products.description: A nonprofit network of therapists who reserve reduced-fee places for people without adequate insurance: pay a one-time membership fee, then see a vetted therapist online or in person at a sliding-scale rate.

privacy.note: Open Path's privacy policy says some business partners use cookies 'to show OPPC; A FUND OF FEMHC ads on other sites on the internet as a result of you using the Site', though it says those cookies do not contain personal information; therapy records themselves sit with your therapist, not the platform.

safety.note: Open Path's FAQ says member therapists must be licensed or provisionally licensed clinicians with a relevant graduate degree, that staff verify licenses and credentials, and that student interns must document a school-approved clinical placement.

economical.note: Open Path says individual sessions cost $40-70 (couples and family $40-80), student-intern sessions $30, after a one-time $65 membership fee, with no recurring fees and all session fees paid to the therapist.

accessibility.note: Open Path operates in the US and Canada, offers online and in-person sessions, and says it serves clients who lack insurance or adequate mental health coverage and cannot afford market rates; you must find and contact a therapist with an opening yourself.

products.name: NHS Talking Therapies
products.description: Free NHS psychological therapy for anxiety and depression in England. You can refer yourself without seeing a GP or having a diagnosis, and treatment can be face-to-face, remote, in groups or digital.

privacy.note: The NHS says that when you refer yourself, the service will 'explain what information will be shared with your GP'; records are held by an NHS service under NHS confidentiality rules rather than a company with an advertising business.

safety.note: NHS England says the services offer a range of NICE-recommended talking therapies delivered by trained psychological therapists and practitioners, and that 670,000 people received a course of treatment in 2023/24. For urgent help the NHS points people to 111 (mental health option), Samaritans on 116 123, or 999 in an emergency.

economical.note: NHS England says the therapies, delivered face-to-face, remotely, individually or in groups, are free for patients to access.

accessibility.note: The NHS says you can refer yourself if you live in England and are 18 or over (16 or 17 in some areas), that you do not need a diagnosed condition, and that some areas accept people not registered with a GP; there can be a wait for a first session, and the service is England-only.

links.label: NHS: where to get urgent help for mental health

products.name: 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline
products.description: The US national crisis line: call, text or chat 988 at any hour for free, confidential support from a trained crisis counselor at a local center. For anyone in distress, not only people thinking about suicide.

privacy.note: The 988 privacy policy says the Lifeline 'does not sell your personal data for money or other consideration', but that it collects your IP address and general location to route the contact, keeps counselor notes and may keep call recordings or transcripts, and may connect someone identified as in immediate danger to 911/Emergency Medical Services; the right to opt out of sharing does not apply if you are at imminent risk.

safety.note: SAMHSA describes 988 as '24/7, free and confidential support to people in suicidal crisis or emotional distress' through the national Lifeline network, and the Lifeline says all counselors complete required core trainings; this is the dedicated crisis route the other options here tell you to use.

economical.note: SAMHSA describes the Lifeline as providing '24/7, free and confidential support', and the Lifeline's own site says conversations are free and confidential.

accessibility.note: The FCC says you reach trained counselors 'By calling or texting 988', that live chat is available at 988lifeline.org, that videophone service is offered for people who use American Sign Language, that voice, text and chat are offered in Spanish, and that veterans can press 1; it also says FCC rules now require wireless carriers to route 988 calls by a caller's general location 'while protecting privacy by not identifying the caller's precise location'. The 988 FAQ adds that TTY users can dial 711 then 988.

products.name: Samaritans
products.description: The UK and Ireland charity helpline: call 116 123 free, any time, to talk to a trained volunteer about anything, without giving your name.

privacy.note: Samaritans says it 'maintains confidentiality even after the death of a caller' except in set situations such as consent or calling an ambulance when a caller appears to be in danger, that you do not have to give your name, and that letters are shredded after a reply is sent.

safety.note: Samaritans offers emotional support from trained volunteers rather than clinicians; it will call an ambulance in some situations, and the NHS lists it as a free listening service for people who need urgent support.

economical.note: Samaritans says 'This number is free to call' from any phone, including pay-as-you-go mobiles with no credit, and that visiting a branch is free.

accessibility.note: Samaritans says you can call 116 123 any time, day or night, visit one of more than 200 branches, or write a letter; its web chat is a small pilot not yet available to everyone, and its email service has closed.

links.label: NHS: where to get urgent help for mental health

products.name: Shout 85258
products.description: A free, confidential 24/7 text service for anyone in the UK who is struggling to cope: text SHOUT to 85258 to reach a trained volunteer.

privacy.note: Shout describes itself as 'Providing people with anonymous and confidential support' and says you can text free and anonymously from all major UK networks; its safeguarding duties mean it may act to protect someone at risk. Crisis Text Line, the US service it is modelled on, points UK users to Shout's own privacy terms.

safety.note: Shout's FAQ says 'Every conversation is overseen by a Clinical Supervisor and assessed for risk' and that volunteers will never close a conversation where there is an imminent risk to life; it is a volunteer de-escalation service, not therapy, and tells people to call 999 if life is at imminent risk.

economical.note: Shout calls itself 'the UK's only free confidential text crisis service', free from all major UK networks.

accessibility.note: Shout's FAQ says anyone of any age resident in the UK can text, aiming to respond within five minutes, from all major UK networks; frequent users may be limited to one conversation every 48 hours after 20 conversations in 60 days.

products.name: Crisis Text Line
products.description: A US nonprofit text and chat line: text HOME to 741741 at any hour to reach a trained volunteer Crisis Counselor. In 2022 it ended a data-sharing arrangement with a for-profit spin-off after public criticism.

privacy.note: Crisis Text Line's privacy policy (updated April 17, 2026) says it keeps a record of each conversation and receives your phone number and carrier, may share identifying data if necessary to prevent death or serious injury, and may share anonymized data with researchers, partners or the public to inform public health, raise awareness 'or for any other reasons'; you can text DELETE to request deletion. History: in January 2022 it ended a data-sharing relationship with the for-profit Loris.ai and asked it to delete the data, the same day FCC Commissioner Brendan Carr wrote asking both to stop.

safety.note: Crisis Text Line connects texters with a 'live volunteer Crisis Counselor' and says it may share identifying information when necessary to prevent death or serious injury; it tells anyone in danger to call 911. Its counselors are trained volunteers rather than clinicians.

economical.note: Crisis Text Line describes itself as '24/7 Free Confidential Mental Health Support'.

accessibility.note: You can text HOME to 741741, use web chat or WhatsApp, at any hour; the service is US-only, with partner services in the UK, Canada and Ireland.

links.label: Crisis Text Line: ending data sharing with Loris (January 2022)
FCC Commissioner Carr letter to Crisis Text Line and Loris.ai (January 2022)
